token_rotation_request_identity.source_level_finding: V16 hashes credential_fingerprint into durable request identity. Rotation from credential A to B for the same principal/session/client/logical request changes the request key and can fragment replay recognition.
proposed_split: CredentialInstance rotatable/revocable and retained as provenance
CurrentAuthorization revalidated before replay disclosure or consequential action
token_rotation_request_identity.strongest_counterhypothesis: Credential-scoped request namespaces are intentional and clients must mint new request IDs after rotation.
token_rotation_request_identity.target_falsifier: On exact accepted target, rotate A to B while holding principal/session/client/request/payload constant. Require REPLAY without a second consequence; require conflict on semantic payload change, isolation across principals, and current-scope/revocation checks on every replay. Add concurrent rotation and crash/restart cases.
token_rotation_request_identity.boundary: Current evidence is source-level/local only; no target runtime pass and no duplicate effect reproduction.

H-RUNTIME-ADMISSION-PROPAGATION-001.note: A correct parent receipt plus correctly mapped expected object did not identify the provider serving pysqlite.

H-DIMENSION-COMPLETE-IDENTITY-001.note: Missing active-provider dimensions caused false merge; volatile credential inclusion causes logical-request fragmentation risk.

new_hypothesis.claim: An admissibility identity must contain all and only stable semantically relevant dimensions: omitting a relevant dimension produces false merges/aliases, while including a rotating incidental dimension produces false splits/fragmentation.
new_hypothesis.counterhypothesis: The SQLite and token cases are unrelated implementation bugs and a shared dimension discipline adds no predictive value.
new_hypothesis.falsifier: Preregister a two-sided matrix. Alias side: same source/version but different active provider must deny. Fragment side: same principal/logical request across credential rotation must replay without a second consequence. Separation controls must still distinguish different principals, payload semantics, runtime providers and current authorization. Reject the concept if one rule cannot predict both error polarities without raising unacceptable false rejections.
